setup: none  -- small VALUES lists execute single-threaded in literal order, so permuting literals permutes accumulation order; multi-statement pins as elsewhere

pins.claim: sum(DOUBLE) is order-sensitive: permuting the same four values changes the answer (1e16 absorbs 1.0) — the epsilon tier exists
pins.query:
SELECT sum(x) FROM (VALUES (1e16),(1.0),(1.0),(-1e16)) t(x)
SELECT sum(x) FROM (VALUES (1e16),(-1e16),(1.0),(1.0)) t(x)

pins.claim: avg(DOUBLE) inherits the same order sensitivity
pins.query:
SELECT avg(x) FROM (VALUES (1e16),(1.0),(1.0),(-1e16)) t(x)
SELECT avg(x) FROM (VALUES (1e16),(-1e16),(1.0),(1.0)) t(x)

pins.claim: sum(BIGINT) is exact and order-insensitive (integer algebra; result is decimal128(38,0) at the Arrow boundary per arrow-export.json)
pins.query:
SELECT sum(x) FROM (VALUES (9007199254740993::BIGINT),(1::BIGINT),(-9007199254740993::BIGINT)) t(x)
SELECT sum(x) FROM (VALUES (1::BIGINT),(9007199254740993::BIGINT),(-9007199254740993::BIGINT)) t(x)

pins.claim: min/max/count over DOUBLE are order-insensitive (selection, not accumulation) — exact tier
pins.query:
SELECT min(x), max(x), count(x) FROM (VALUES (1e16),(1.0),(-1e16)) t(x)
SELECT min(x), max(x), count(x) FROM (VALUES (-1e16),(1e16),(1.0)) t(x)

pins.claim: stddev_pop(DOUBLE) permutation probe: this permutation did NOT expose order sensitivity — insufficient to move stddev out of the epsilon tier (accumulation is still floating-point; absence of a counterexample here is not a proof)
pins.query:
SELECT stddev_pop(x) FROM (VALUES (1e16),(1.0),(1.0),(-1e16)) t(x)
SELECT stddev_pop(x) FROM (VALUES (1e16),(-1e16),(1.0),(1.0)) t(x)

pins.claim: Bare decimal literals make 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.3 TRUE in DuckDB (DECIMAL arithmetic); the same comparison over DOUBLE is FALSE — the classic float identity needs explicit casts to observe
quantize via the f32 grid: CAST(CAST(x AS FLOAT) AS DOUBLE) collapses epsilon-different DOUBLE inputs to one value (the pack_trees trick as a plan node)
pins.query: SELECT CAST(CAST(0.1::DOUBLE + 0.2::DOUBLE AS FLOAT) AS DOUBLE) = CAST(CAST(0.3::DOUBLE AS FLOAT) AS DOUBLE)
